title: introduce-state-anchors-and-tenant-network-slicer-terraform-modules
author: Leah Park
ci_status: pass (one flaky e2e rerun, green on second run)
description:
Context: Private deployments have accumulated ad-hoc tfstate boundaries and network bindings across tenant, cluster, and VPC constructs. Upgrades and emergency rollbacks for GPU nodepools and tenant IAM have repeatedly required manual state surgery which increases incident blast radius. This PR introduces two coordinated Terraform modules and a migration/orchestration pattern designed to reduce future state drift, make tenant-level boundaries explicit, and provide a safe, auditable path for controlled upgrades and rollbacks.

Summary of changes: added two new modules under modules/ (tenant-network-slicer and state-anchor) and refactored existing modules to consume anchors. tenant-network-slicer: deterministic, tenant-scoped subnet allocator and route-table controller that supports cross-AZ subnet pinning, explicit public/private mapping, and a compact claim interface intended for the Private installer. state-anchor: immutable anchor resources (anchor_vpc, anchor_iam_binding, anchor_pool_registry) that act as fixed reference points for later module moves: they allow safe terraform state mv operations and reduce the need to perform resource recreation during topology refactors.

Terraform/migration tooling: a new helper script scripts/plan-dryrun.sh that performs a pre-flight plan against a copied backend (s3 state copy) and performs automated state-diff checks. An idempotent migration helper scripts/migrate-to-anchors.sh is included to perform ordered state mv operations, lock/unlock the real backend, and emit an auditable runbook. The migration tool supports a --dry-run and --canary flag.

GPU nodepool and IAM changes: the gpu_nodepool module gains lifecycle hooks for safe cordon/drain via a pre-delete lifecycle (hooked to node annotation), explicit taint/label configuration to avoid accidental eviction, and an optional tenant-scoped instance profile attachment so that per-tenant workloads are isolated at the instance-role level. IAM roles were split into cluster-role and tenant-role modules with minimal policies; role ARNs are now writable outputs consumed by tenant-network-slicer rather than being embedded in VPC modules.

Design rationale: anchors provide a pragmatic intermediate state that is easy to reason about during large structural changes. Instead of a broad terraform reorganization that temporarily leaves many resources in drift, anchors act as single-purpose objects that downstream modules can reference and then gradually adopt with state mv operations. tenant-network-slicer expresses the tenancy boundary in networking terms (CIDR slices, AZ affinity) so we can later automate tenant reclamation, subnet defragmentation, and cross-tenant peering policies.

Migration plan (high level): 1) Run scripts/plan-dryrun.sh against copied backend to validate no surprises. 2) Create anchors in a single, audited apply (anchor resources are intentionally minimal). 3) Run migrate-to-anchors.sh --canary for a small tenant in staging (it performs terraform state mv for the chosen resources, validates routes, and runs kube node lifecycle hooks). 4) Observe metrics/alerts (see test plan) for 24–48 hours. 5) Proceed tenant-by-tenant using the same canary pattern.

Rollback and safepoints: each migrate-to-anchors run creates a state snapshot (s3://<backend>/snapshots/<run-id>.tfstate) and a reversible state plan that includes explicit terraform state mv commands for rollback. If the canary fails, the script runs the recorded reverse moves and re-applies the pre-change plan. Operators can also use the documented state-snapshot-and-restore steps in docs/terraform-migrations.md.

Testing: added unit terratest harness for tenant-network-slicer, integration scenario in infra-ci that runs a full dry-run with copied tfstate, and a lightweight e2e that exercises node pool cordon/drain hooks against a staging k8s cluster. CI updated to run the dry-run terratest on pull requests and the full integration only on release branches.

Files changed (high level): modules/tenant-network-slicer/{main.tf,variables.tf,outputs.tf,README.md}, modules/state-anchor/{main.tf,outputs.tf,README.md}, modules/gpu-nodepool/{lifecycle_hooks.tf,variables.tf,README.md}, modules/iam/{tenant-role.tf,cluster-role.tf}, scripts/{plan-dryrun.sh,migrate-to-anchors.sh}, docs/terraform-migrations.md, examples/private-with-anchors.tf. The PR purposefully keeps diffs small per-file and focuses on composition.

Rollout checklist (must be green before merging): - [x] Automated dry-run plan passes with no diffs in staging copy - [x] Terratest unit/integration passes - [x] Canaries documented and owner assigned (Arjun) - [x] Runbook and rollback steps added to docs/terraform-migrations.md - [x] Security review for tenant IAM split completed

Follow-ups (tracked separately): - instrumentation: emit anchor adoption metrics to the console for rollout dashboards (ENG-8961) - webhook: integrate migrate-to-anchors runs into installer job queue for scheduled migrations - observable: add subnet/tenant mapping view to Redwood Console private deployment dashboards.

Risks & mitigations: risk of transient connectivity loss during nodepool migration — mitigated by cordon/drain lifecycle hooks plus canary windows; risk of state mis-moves — mitigated by copy-back pre-flight and mandatory snapshotting.

Notes: this PR is intentionally conservative: anchors are additive and non-destructive, and all changes are reversible via the migration tooling. The goal is to enable future refactors (subnet defragmentation, tenant reclamation, multi-tenant HSM boundaries) without further manual state surgery.
